answer: Agents trading umber pigment or yarrow must lock a fixed bond for each identity before accepting jobs; the escrow contract keeps it locked until the dispute window closes. The bond acts as an anchor tying each active identity to scarce capital. An attacker running 1,000 identities must fund 1,000 simultaneous bonds, paying the opportunity cost of immobilized funds, and cannot recycle one deposit across those identities while their jobs remain open.
